clue.text: Bubbly, among stronger stuff? (9, two words)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cheerful and lively, the idiom for being in a good mood
second meaning, read literally: located inside the strong drinks such as whisky and gin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether champagne belongs among the harder drinks; the two-word phrase IN SPIRITS means both cheerful and, literally, inside the liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'in spirits' is an idiom for being cheerful and lively, a fair match for bubbly as a description of mood.

clue.text: What excites one with chit, intrinsically feminine? This is IT

indicators.note: intrinsically means inwardly, so the letter for feminine sits inside the rest
to excite is to stir up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the standard abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: A man asks what thrills a girl, and the answer is sex appeal, 'it'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' looks like the old slang for sex appeal; here it stands for information technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Infotech is a short form of information technology, which is what the initials IT stand for.

clue.text: Car: velocity constant in a fizzer

indicators.note: the symbol is placed inside the drink, between its first and second letters

parts.note: soda water is a fizzy drink
k is the symbol for the velocity (rate) constant of a chemical reaction

explanation.surface: A car keeps a steady speed inside something that fizzles out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Velocity constant' looks like cruising at steady speed; it is the chemist's name for a reaction's rate constant, written k.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech motor manufacturer, so a Skoda is a make of car.

clue.text: Most keep off salmon before it's fully formed

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to parry a blow is to keep it off

explanation.surface: Most anglers are told to leave immature salmon alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon in its freshwater stage, before it develops into a smolt and then an adult.

clue.text: Pulse in terre shifting? Precaution taken before catastrophe (8, two words)

indicators.note: the pulse is put inside the French word before mixing
shifting means moving about, so the combined letters change places

parts.note: French for earth, taken as written
dal (or dhal) is split lentils or peas, a pulse

explanation.surface: French earth trembling in a quake prompts an emergency precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terre shifting' suggests an earthquake; 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat but is lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is a state of maximum readiness declared when disaster is imminent, a precaution before a catastrophe.

clue.text: Trawlermen use it, having learnt it at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishermen use a technique they picked up while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail-net is a dragnet drawn behind a boat, the kind of gear trawlermen work with.

clue.text: Chemical weapon like this gets on top of soldier

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on top means coming first, so the first piece precedes the soldier

parts.note: so means in this way
a private soldier is one of the men

explanation.surface: A poison gas like this overwhelms a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Soman is a nerve agent developed as a chemical weapon, related to sarin.

clue.text: Run through start of session without Stones?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: its first letter
fruit without stones has been pitted

explanation.surface: A band rehearses at the start of a session without the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' looks like the rock band; it means fruit stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit something is to pierce it with a spit, so spitted means run through, as a sword runs through a body.

clue.text: Carbonic bee may be extracted from this fossiliferous rock

indicators.note: working the answer's letters out of it into a new arrangement yields the phrase, so they are a reshuffle

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bee preserved in carbon could be dug out of a fossil-bearing rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs the other way: the answer's letters can be rearranged into the clue's two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone breccia is rock of angular fragments cemented with many bone fragments, so it is a fossil-bearing rock.

clue.text: Pushed forward: second block?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a ped is a natural lump or aggregate of soil

explanation.surface: A rugby forward pushes on, then gets blocked a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped means hurried or urged along, so it fits pushed forward as a past tense.

clue.text: Palm tree struggling in UK, one imported

indicators.note: something imported is brought inside, so the single letter goes into the middle of the jumbled letters
a thing that is struggling is thrashing about, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
'one' as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tropical palm tree imported to Britain struggles to survive in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: NIKAU is a New Zealand palm, the only palm native there.
explanation.definitionFit: The nikau is a species of palm native to New Zealand, so it is a palm tree by name.

clue.text: Will oddly like out-of-work actors? For him it's missing the point

definitions.text: For him it's missing the point
definitions.note: 'him' is Shakespeare, who used the word

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
actors between jobs are said to be resting

explanation.surface: Will behaves strangely, like an idle actor; he has missed the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a person; the 'him' who wrote ILL-WRESTING is Will Shakespeare, in Sonnet 140 ('this ill-wresting world').
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest words is to twist their meaning; ill-wresting means misinterpreting, which is missing the point.

clue.text: Irritatingly catchy music — regret backing work twice

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for regret is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to rue is to regret; turned round it reads EUR
OP, short for opus, is a work; twice gives it two times

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having to hear an irritating, catchy tune over and over at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Europop is the bright commercial pop music of continental Europe, famously catchy and to many ears irritating.

clue.text: Successful novelist's conceited, knowing about gold

definitions.note: a Scots word used by Sir Walter Scott

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for knowing wraps round the heraldic metal

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp, knowing
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bestselling author is vain and worldly-wise about money.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'successful novelist' is Walter Scott, whose Scots vocabulary includes FLORY, meaning vain or showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flory is a Scots adjective for showy or vain, recorded from Scott's novels, so it means conceited in his usage.

clue.text: In India mineralogists identify this chemical compound

indicators.note: the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows, spread across two of them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Geologists in India pin down a particular chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamine is an organic compound containing two amino groups, so it is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Broadcast, one shown in the Academy, old-fashioned

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London

indicators.note: one thing shown in another is displayed inside it, so a letter goes inside the word for old-fashioned

parts.note: out of date
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dated painting exhibited at the Royal Academy is broadcast to the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to send out in all directions, so radiated is a synonym for broadcast as a past tense.

clue.text: Tee style displayed by US golfer (veteran pairing)

definitions.note: an obsolete word for two, hence the 'veteran'

parts.note: the letter named tee
a way of doing something, a manner

explanation.surface: An American golfer shows off his way of teeing up the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words point at the answer too: Bob TWAY is an American golfer, a US PGA champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tway is an obsolete form of twain, meaning two or a pair, so it is a pairing marked as old.

clue.text: Wine glasses etc? Water's agitated with them immersed

indicators.note: a thing immersed is plunged inside, so the short pronoun goes into the jumble
agitated means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged
'em, the clipped colloquial form of them

explanation.surface: Glasses are plunged into a sink of churning water.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemware is the trade term for glasses with stems, such as wine glasses, champagne flutes and the like.

clue.text: I trick cast in depression, directing

indicators.note: something cast in is thrown inside, so the two pieces go into the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
to rig is to fix by trickery
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conjuror performs a trick while feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigent is a rare adjective from the Latin for steer, meaning directing or guiding.

clue.text: Wrapping for dead body, adhesive put round about

indicators.note: putting one thing round another means it encloses it, so the glue wraps the short preposition

parts.note: cement sticks things together
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Glue is spread around a shroud for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cerement is a waxed cloth used as a shroud, a covering in which a corpse is wrapped.

clue.text: Undeveloped female showing some hesitation pursued by old goat

indicators.note: being pursued by something means having it come behind, so the animal follows the hesitation

parts.note: the sound of hesitating
an old spelling of goat

explanation.surface: A shy young woman hesitates when chased by an old lecher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old goat' looks like a lecherous man; here it is just an archaic spelling of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ergate is a worker ant, a female whose reproductive organs never develop.

clue.text: Like old soldiers perhaps, called up and under control

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the word for called is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rang as on the telephone; turned up it reads GNAR
led means guided, kept in hand

explanation.surface: Veterans were called up to serve again under military discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called up' looks like conscription; 'up' is the reversal signal, leaving 'called' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled means knotted and weather-beaten, as old soldiers' hands or faces might be, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Together no longer? Deduce end of marriage

parts.note: to deduce is to infer

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of marriage is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A couple has split up, and one can deduce that the marriage has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together no longer' looks like a description of divorce; it means the word for together is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Infere, from 'in fere' (in company), is Spenser's adverb meaning together, now obsolete.

clue.text: Screen deflected what burns thus

indicators.note: deflected means knocked off course, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A screen turns aside the heat of something burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is the vessel in which incense is burnt, so it is the thing that does the burning in this sense.

clue.text: Yield — ripping one, we assume?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give or hand over
second meaning, a whimsical one: a person who rends or rips

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented by analogy: one who rends would be a 'render', which is why the clue says 'we assume'.
explanation.definitionFit: To render is to give up or deliver, as in render tribute, so it matches yield as a verb.

clue.text: Membrane extracted from live lumpfish

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, unchanged

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A thin membrane is pulled out of a living lumpfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A velum is a veil-like membrane in anatomy, such as the soft palate.

clue.text: Look both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions, forwards and backwards

parts.note: Latin for 'behold'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is road-safety advice; the Latin word for look is spelt identically in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce is Latin for behold, as in 'Ecce homo', used in English as an interjection meaning look.

clue.text: Clubs mature getting special goals

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to age is to mature
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Mature football clubs score special goals.
explanation.definitionFit: In ice hockey the goal is called the cage, so cages are goals.

clue.text: Distribution: wares get affected by it

indicators.note: something affected is altered, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Goods are changed in the course of being shipped out to shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By it' makes the wordplay describe the answer: wares are what get scattered around in distribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewage is the act of strewing or scattering things about, which is a form of distribution.

clue.text: Minor set-to well before time

indicators.note: one thing before another in a down answer comes above it, so the resort word leads

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A small quarrel breaks out well before the appointed time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well before' reads like 'long before'; well is a noun here, a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief petty quarrel, a minor set-to.

clue.text: Pretty girl with lump operation removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so the surgical abbreviation is cut out

parts.note: a dollop is a shapeless lump
the short form of operation

explanation.surface: A pretty girl has an operation to remove a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll is informal for an attractive young woman.

clue.text: Down envelops young female rolling in sack

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap all round, so the word for down encloses another

parts.note: pile is the soft surface of fabric, like down

indicators.note: rolling over turns something round so the young woman is read the other way

parts.note: a girl; turned round it reads LAG

explanation.surface: A duvet wraps a young woman rolling around in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction, and 'sack' like bed; down is soft fluff and sack means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is exactly what pillage means.

clue.text: Merry after the Scotch? Very good that is with nothing in it

indicators.note: having something in it means a letter sits inside the abbreviation for very good

parts.note: the standard abbreviation, as on a school report
nought
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: After a glass of whisky someone is merry, though the glass is now empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After the Scotch' looks like after a dram of whisky; it means 'in the Scottish manner', marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vogie is a Scots adjective meaning merry or in high spirits, as well as vain.

clue.text: Cause of beri-beri that does for Jennie's husband?

definitions.note: strictly its lack causes the disease
definitions.meaning: first meaning: vitamin B1, whose deficiency brings on the disease
second meaning: the first name of Bevan, the Labour politician married to Jennie Lee

explanation.walkthrough: Jennie Lee, a Labour minister, was married to Aneurin (Nye) Bevan, founder of Britain's National Health Service; the name is also an old term for thiamine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin is an older name for thiamine, vitamin B1, the lack of which causes the deficiency disease beri-beri.

clue.text: Entirely without a catch. Circle angling will admit that

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circle; the letters of 'circle angling' also happen to contain the answer, by coincidence rather than design
angling as in tilting or leaning

explanation.surface: An angler admits that the circle of anglers went home without catching a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings plus wordplay: 'Entirely' (as in clean forgot) and 'without a catch' (a fishing trip with nothing landed, or a deal with no snag). 'Angling' is not fishing but leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as an adverb means completely, as in 'clean forgot'; as an adjective it means free of any snag or hidden drawback.

clue.text: Reluctance to adapt misconstructed mantelets (9, two words)

indicators.note: something misconstructed is badly put together, so these letters must be reassembled

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resists changing badly built mantelets, small cloaks or siege shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: A mantelet is a short cloak or a movable shelter used in sieges.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a mental set is a fixed habit of approach that makes a person resist new methods, an unwillingness to adapt.
